purpose: Fix 8 security/privacy audit findings including shell injection, credential exposure, temp file leaks, non-atomic writes, path traversal hardening, and duplicated sanitization logic across lib, action, and config files.
riskRationale: All core security fixes (shell injection, credential redaction, atomic writes, path traversal guard) are correctly implemented. Two important issues remain but are one-line fixes with no architectural impact. Confidence in the rest of the codebase is high.

text: Well-structured PR with clean, scoped fixes per audit finding. The critical shell injection fix (execFileSync for taskkill), consolidated sanitizeString utility, atomic JSON writes (write-to-temp-then-rename), path traversal guard via path.relative(), and askpass cleanup are all implemented correctly. However, 2 important and 4 minor issues persist from previous review iterations.

reasoning: 2 important issues remain: (1) path.resolve() does not resolve symlinks in the path traversal guard; (2) Bearer token regex is missing Base64 padding characters and uses a case-insensitive flag causing false positives. Both have straightforward single-line fixes.

message: Correctly replaced cp.execSync with cp.execFileSync for taskkill, eliminating shell injection via argument array.

Consolidated duplicate sanitization logic from logger.ts and action/src/utils.ts into a single shared utility with descriptive redaction labels, ensuring consistent credential redaction across all output channels.
Both flushSync and writeToDisk now use write-to-temp-then-rename, providing atomic file persistence that prevents data corruption on crash.
Using path.relative() instead of startsWith prefix checking properly handles path-normalization attacks (e.g., /home/user-evil no longer bypasses the trusted-directory check).
Added process.on('exit') cleanup for askpass temp directories and removed chmodSync 0o755 overrides, preserving 0o700 from writeFileSync.
Removed PRIVATE_KEY inline field and updated comment to discourage pasting secrets directly into .env files.
sanitizeDbError wraps credential-bearing connection error messages with a URI-based redactor, preventing credential leakage in logs and exceptions.

path.resolve() does not resolve symlinks. A git config --show-origin entry containing a symlink (e.g., .gitconfig symlinking to /etc/passwd) would pass the path.relative() guard because path.resolve only normalizes '.' and '..' but does not follow symlinks.
suggestion: Use fs.realpathSync(cfg) instead of path.resolve(cfg) to resolve symlinks before the path traversal check. fs.realpathSync follows all symlinks and returns the canonical absolute path.

message: The Bearer token regex has two issues: (1) the character class [a-zA-Z0-9._\-+/]+ does not include =, so standard Base64 padding characters leak in logs; (2) the /gi flag matches lowercase 'bearer ' in prose text, causing false positive redactions.
suggestion: Add = to the character class for Base64 padding coverage and drop the i flag since the HTTP Authorization header is standardized as case-sensitive 'Bearer'.

message: sanitizeString is exported as a public API from lib/src/index.ts but has no JSDoc documenting what patterns it redacts or when to use it.
suggestion: Add JSDoc describing the function, the token patterns it redacts (GitHub tokens, OpenAI keys, Anthropic keys, Slack tokens, Bearer tokens, env-var patterns), and its intended usage context (log/error sanitization).

message: If the process crashes between writeFileSync(tmpPath) and renameSync(tmpPath, filePath), a stale .tmp file remains. While this does not cause data loss, it could accumulate over many restarts.
suggestion: Clean up stale .tmp files at the start of the load() method by checking for and removing any existing .tmp file associated with the target path before reading.

message: The process.on('exit') handler only cleans up the last assigned askPassDir. If configureGit() is called multiple times, earlier temp directories are orphaned until process exit. The 'exit' event also does not fire on SIGKILL.
suggestion: Consider adding SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that invoke cleanup, and either track all created directories in an array or reuse the existing askPassDir on subsequent calls.

message: The regex [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]+:// matches any URI scheme including file://. An error message containing file:///path/@something would incorrectly redact the path portion. Benign in practice since DB errors rarely contain file:// URIs, but could confuse debugging.
suggestion: Narrow the regex to only match known DB connection schemes (postgres://, mysql://, mongodb://) to eliminate false positives on file:// URIs.
